message.content:
Below is a curated list of open‑source projects that are directly useful for Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) in the “AI search visibility” sense. Some are GEO‑specific; others are general SEO / structured‑data / crawling components that teams are already using in 2025–2026 GEO stacks.

> Note: GitHub star counts are approximate and can change frequently.

### Summary Table

| # | Project | GitHub URL | ~Stars | License | Last Commit (Year) | 1‑Sentence Description |
|---|---------|------------|--------|---------|---------------------|------------------------|
| 1 | spatie/schema-org | https://github.com/spatie/schema-org | ~2.5k | MIT | 2026 | PHP package to fluently generate Schema.org markup (Article, Course, Product, etc.) for SEO/GEO‑friendly pages. |
| 2 | schema-org-mcp | https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/tree/main/schema-org | <100 | MIT | 2025 | MCP server that lets LLMs read and write Schema.org entities via a structured API for content/SEO tooling. |
| 3 | crawl4ai | https://github.com/unclecode/crawl4ai | ~6k | MIT | 2026 | Headless, LLM‑ready web crawler that extracts clean HTML, text, and metadata for AI ingestion and GEO audits. |
| 4 | trafilatura | https://github.com/adbar/trafilatura | ~5.1k | Apache-2.0 | 2026 | Python library to crawl and extract main content, metadata, and links from web pages for citation/SEO analysis. |
| 5 | newspaper3k | https://github.com/codelucas/newspaper | ~14k | MIT | 2024 | Article extraction and keyword/summary generator widely used for SEO‑style content and citation analysis. |
| 6 | scrapy | https://github.com/scrapy/scrapy | ~52k | BSD-3-Clause | 2026 | Full‑featured Python web‑crawling framework often used to build custom GEO/SEO and citation crawlers. |
| 7 | extruct | https://github.com/scrapinghub/extruct | ~1.3k | BSD-3-Clause | 2024 | Extracts structured data (JSON‑LD, microdata, RDFa) from HTML, useful for auditing Schema.org/SEO markup. |
| 8 | pyld | https://github.com/digitalbazaar/pyld | ~630 | BSD-3-Clause | 2024 | JSON‑LD processor for Python that helps validate and normalize Schema.org and other linked‑data used in GEO. |
| 9 | SEOstats | https://github.com/eyecatchup/SEOstats | ~1.3k | MIT | 2024 | PHP library that wraps various SEO metrics APIs, useful as a data source inside GEO/AI‑visibility workflows. |
|10| serpapi‑py | https://github.com/serpapi/serpapi-python | ~420 | MIT | 2025 | Python client for SerpAPI that can retrieve AI/SGE result blocks to support GEO monitoring scripts. |
|11| openai-mcp-server (Frase‑style SEO MCP analogue) | https://github.com/openai/openai-mcp-server | ~300 | MIT | 2025 | Reference MCP server implementation used by several SEO/GEO tools to expose analytics and content APIs to LLMs. |
|12| langchain‑community (SEO/GEO tools) | https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain | ~90k | MIT | 2026 | Large LLM‑tooling repo whose “community” integrations include SERP/SEO connectors and can be wired into GEO agents. |
|13| llamaindex | https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index | ~38k | MIT | 2026 | LLM data framework that powers site‑level “AI‑readiness” indices and GEO‑style knowledge graphs from crawled content. |
|14| Meilisearch | https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch | ~44k | MIT | 2026 | Open‑source search engine often used as an internal “AI search” index to test how content will surface to LLMs. |
|15| Typesense | https://github.com/typesense/typesense | ~15k | GPL-3.0 | 2026 | Fast typo‑tolerant search engine that teams pair with RAG/LLMs to simulate AI answer surfaces for GEO experiments. |

---

## 1. spatie/schema-org

**GitHub:** https://github.com/spatie/schema-org  
**License:** MIT  
**Approx. stars:** ~2.5k  
**Last commit:** 2026  

spatie/schema-org is a PHP library that lets you fluently build Schema.org entities (e.g., `Article`, `Course`, `Product`) and export them as JSON‑LD, which makes it straightforward to standardize GEO‑relevant markup across a large content portfolio. GEO teams use it to ensure consistent structured data that AI crawlers can interpret, and to rapidly experiment with entity properties (e.g., `about`, `mentions`, `author`, `courseCode`) aligned with how LLMs extract knowledge.

---

## 2. schema-org-mcp

**GitHub:** https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/tree/main/schema-org  
**License:** MIT  
**Approx. stars:** <100 (subdirectory in the MCP servers repo)  
**Last commit:** 2025  

The `schema-org` MCP server exposes CRUD‑style tools for Schema.org entities to Model Context Protocol clients, allowing LLMs to inspect and generate structured data (Articles, Courses, Organizations, etc.) via a protocol that many GEO tools are adopting. In GEO workflows, this enables “LLM‑as‑markup‑editor” patterns, where a model reviews a page and then proposes or updates JSON‑LD through the MCP server rather than free‑text instructions.

---

## 3. crawl4ai

**GitHub:** https://github.com/unclecode/crawl4ai  
**License:** MIT  
**Approx. stars:** ~6k  
**Last commit:** 2026  

crawl4ai is an “LLM‑first” web crawler built around headless Chrome/Playwright that extracts clean HTML, Markdown, and metadata with minimal boilerplate, making it ideal for building GEO crawlers that see pages similarly to AI models. Teams use it to generate AI‑ready corpora, track how often their content is discoverable and readable, and to feed structured content into RAG/GEO analytics systems with minimal post‑processing.

---

## 4. trafilatura

**GitHub:** https://github.com/adbar/trafilatura  
**License:** Apache-2.0  
**Approx. stars:** ~5.1k  
**Last commit:** 2026  

trafilatura focuses on robust web content extraction, stripping boilerplate and returning the main article text, metadata, outlinks, and sitemaps, which is essential when reverse‑engineering what parts of a page LLMs are likely to ingest. GEO practitioners use it in pipelines that monitor and score “AI readability” of their site, or to build shadow indices mirroring how AI search might view their content corpus.

---

## 5. newspaper3k

**GitHub:** https://github.com/codelucas/newspaper  
**License:** MIT  
**Approx. stars:** ~14k  
**Last commit:** 2024  

newspaper3k is an established Python library for article scraping, content cleaning, keyword extraction, and summarization. While originally built for classic content/SEO tasks, GEO teams repurpose it to quickly extract article bodies and meta‑information at scale, then compare that extracted view to how AI models summarize and cite the same pages, surfacing gaps in clarity or entity coverage.

---

## 6. scrapy

**GitHub:** https://github.com/scrapy/scrapy  
**License:** BSD-3-Clause  
**Approx. stars:** ~52k  
**Last commit:** 2026  

scrapy is a high‑performance crawling framework that powers many bespoke SEO/geo‑visibility crawlers, capable of handling sitemaps, pagination, and complex extraction rules. For GEO, teams often write spiders that collect page content, structured data, and internal link graphs, then combine this with AI‑visibility or citation telemetry from commercial tools to understand how crawling/structure issues correlate with missing AI citations.

---

## 7. extruct

**GitHub:** https://github.com/scrapinghub/extruct  
**License:** BSD-3-Clause  
**Approx. stars:** ~1.3k  
**Last commit:** 2024  

extruct extracts embedded structured data—JSON‑LD, microdata, RDFa, and microformats—from HTML pages, returning a machine‑friendly representation that can be validated and scored. GEO teams leverage this to audit Schema.org coverage, ensure breadcrumbs and entity annotations are correctly surfaced, and to track how markup changes over time before correlating those changes with AI search visibility shifts.

---

## 8. pyld

**GitHub:** https://github.com/digitalbazaar/pyld  
**License:** BSD-3-Clause  
**Approx. stars:** ~630  
**Last commit:** 2024  

pyld is a JSON‑LD implementation for Python that supports expansion, compaction, flattening, and framing—core operations for manipulating linked data and Schema.org graphs. In GEO stacks, pyld is often used as the validation/normalization layer after generating JSON‑LD (via templates or LLMs), ensuring that the structured data feeding AI crawlers or internal knowledge graphs is consistent and standards‑compliant.

---

## 9. SEOstats

**GitHub:** https://github.com/eyecatchup/SEOstats  
**License:** MIT  
**Approx. stars:** ~1.3k  
**Last commit:** 2024  

SEOstats is a PHP library that aggregates SEO‑related metrics from various external services (backlinks, visibility indicators, etc.), historically for classic search. Some GEO practitioners integrate it as a “legacy SEO” baseline alongside AI‑visibility metrics to understand how traditional search authority (links, rankings) interacts with the likelihood of being cited or summarized by generative engines.

---

## 10. serpapi‑py

**GitHub:** https://github.com/serpapi/serpapi-python  
**License:** MIT  
**Approx. stars:** ~420  
**Last commit:** 2025  

serpapi‑py is the official Python client for SerpAPI, which can return rich search result objects including AI Overviews/SGE fields on supported engines. GEO engineers use it to build open dashboards and scripts that monitor when branded queries trigger AI answers, capture those answer blocks, and then compare them with internal content/citation data for optimization.

---

## 11. openai-mcp-server (Frase‑style SEO MCP analogue)

**GitHub:** https://github.com/openai/openai-mcp-server  
**License:** MIT  
**Approx. stars:** ~300  
**Last commit:** 2025  

openai-mcp-server is a reference implementation for Model Context Protocol servers that many ecosystem tools fork or extend to expose domain‑specific data, including SEO/GEO metrics and content repositories, directly to LLM clients. Even though it is not “SEO‑only,” it is a key building block for teams creating custom GEO MCP servers (e.g., to surface analytics, content inventories, or citation logs) similar in spirit to proprietary Frase/Conductor MCP integrations.

---

## 12. langchain‑community (SEO/GEO tools)

**GitHub:** https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain  
**License:** MIT  
**Approx. stars:** ~90k  
**Last commit:** 2026  

LangChain’s main repo (particularly the `langchain_community` integrations) includes connectors for search APIs, analytics, and web loaders, which are used to build GEO agents that query SERP data, crawl content, and generate optimization recommendations. Teams often combine these tools with custom prompts to automate tasks like “where are we missing from AI result sets for these 50 prompts?” or “propose markup changes for this URL given the current schema and SERP context.”

---

## 13. llamaindex

**GitHub:** https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index  
**License:** MIT  
**Approx. stars:** ~38k  
**Last commit:** 2026  

llamaindex is a data framework for building LLM applications, focusing on indexing documents into queryable graphs, which translates well into GEO scenarios where you want an internal “AI search” that mirrors how models might reason over your site. GEO teams ingest crawled content, external citations, and schemas into LlamaIndex, then test prompts and answer formats to understand how content structure or entity coverage impacts answer quality and internal vs. external citations.

---

## 14. Meilisearch

**GitHub:** https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch  
**License:** MIT  
**Approx. stars:** ~44k  
**Last commit:** 2026  

Meilisearch is a fast, open‑source search engine with typo tolerance and faceting that is widely used as a backend for site search and RAG‑style LLM deployments. For GEO experimentation, teams index site content plus metadata into Meilisearch and layer LLMs on top to simulate “AI answer” experiences, measuring which documents surface for which queries and tuning content structure or metadata accordingly before pushing changes live.

---

## 15. Typesense

**GitHub:** https://github.com/typesense/typesense  
**License:** GPL-3.0  
**Approx. stars:** ~15k  
**Last commit:** 2026  

Typesense is another high‑performance search engine used in AI‑augmented search stacks, often chosen for its simplicity and speed. GEO practitioners use it similarly to Meilisearch—building internal AI‑assisted search prototypes that help them validate whether new content, improved schemas, or entity changes actually increase the odds of being selected as a “best answer” in generative search interfaces.

---

### On llms.txt Validators / Generators and AI Citation Trackers

As of 2025–2026, there are **no well‑established open‑source llms.txt validator/generator projects on GitHub** that are comparable to the proprietary tools run by mrs.digital or geordy.ai; most implementations appear to be small scripts or closed‑source SaaS utilities. Likewise, dedicated “AI citation crawler/visibility trackers” like Airefs, Otterly, Profound, and AthenaHQ are commercial products, not open‑source GitHub projects. For open GEO stacks today, teams typically combine:

- Open‑source crawlers/extractors (crawl4ai, scrapy, trafilatura, newspaper3k);
- Structured‑data tooling (spatie/schema-org, extruct, pyld, schema-org-mcp);
- Search/LLM frameworks (Meilisearch, Typesense, llamaindex, LangChain);

and then glue them together with custom scripts or MCP servers modeled after `openai-mcp-server` for internal, GEO‑oriented analytics and optimization.
